description: What a competent reviewer should say about `flawed-cart.js`, declared before any provider is asked. Scoring a canary against criteria written after reading the answer would measure nothing, so these are committed first and the fixture is not to be repaired.

scoring.required: A provider earns a pass only by naming every defect in `mustFind`. These are unambiguous and present in four lines of code; missing one is not a near miss.
scoring.invention: A finding that names a defect not in `mustFind` and not defensible against the fixture counts as invented. A reviewer that invents findings is worse than no reviewer, because its output has to be checked line by line.
scoring.note: Passing this earns the `code-reviewer` role on synthetic material for the exact provider and model that ran it. It earns nothing else — not implementation, not architecture, not security, not another model from the same vendor.

mustFind.summary: `items` is used without validation, so an undefined or non-array argument throws inside `.reduce`.
`fetchDiscount()` is not awaited, so a promise is subtracted from a number and the result is NaN.
The catch block returns `{ saved: true }`, so a failed write is reported as a successful one.
`repeat` is untrusted and unbounded, so a large value allocates without limit.
